_comment: What the launcher installs and where it gets it. constants.py reads this and keeps the previous hardcoded values as fallbacks, so a missing or malformed catalog degrades to the shipped defaults rather than breaking a launch.

download._comment: Only these registrable domains may serve launcher content; a redirect anywhere else aborts the download before a byte is written. Matched by suffix, so the leading dot in the comparison is what stops evil-huggingface.co from qualifying.

modpack._comment: The client mod set, installed from Modrinth on first run instead of being bundled with the installer. Pinning the exact version and its SHA-512 is what makes the install reproducible: the launcher never asks an API 'what is latest', so a compromised or simply changed upstream cannot alter what a given build installs. Bump version+url+sha512 together to move the pack forward.
modpack.name: Fabulously Optimized

extra_mods._comment: The world server runs offline-mode, so it never sends a skin texture and every player renders as the default Steve however they signed in. CustomSkinLoader fixes that entirely on the client by looking the skin up from Mojang by username, which keeps the server itself vanilla.
extra_mods.name: CustomSkinLoader

resources.description: The castle, its grounds and the whole adventure.

resources.name: Resource Pack
resources.description: Textures, models and sounds the map is built around.

provisioning._comment: Optional. Lets the Azure application id be rotated without shipping a new build. NOT a confidentiality mechanism - a public-client app id is public by design; see launcher_core/provisioning.py. Leave manifest_url empty to switch the whole feature off (the default): the build-time embedded value is then the only source.
provisioning._setup: python tools/sign_manifest.py --new-key   then   --sign client-id.json. Publish the .json and .json.sig, put the printed public key below.

server_properties._comment: Forced into server.properties on every launch (launcher_core/server_manager.py). The first block is security - server-ip is the one that decides whether the neighbours can join. The second block is what makes a local world behave like a singleplayer one: every command a singleplayer world with cheats allows, plus flight, which vanilla otherwise kicks you for.
server_properties._broadcast_comment: The player is an operator now, and op broadcast turns every command block firing in the castle into chat spam.

disk._comment: Used by the first-run system check. client_mb covers the Minecraft client, the mods and a downloaded Java runtime.
